newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh opposition chief reaffirms boycott.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh opposition chief reaffirms boycott.

text.p: Former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia reaffirmed on Monday that her opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) would continue a boycott of parliament indefinitely.

"We have stated clearly that BNP members will continue to abstain from parliament until and unless the speaker and the government are able to satisfy our requirements and demands," Khaleda said while visiting Savar, a township 40 km (25 miles) north of Dhaka.
A BNP youth leader, Moksed Ali Manju, was hacked to death at Savar two days ago, which Khaleda's party blamed on the ruling Awami League.
"They are training guns at us...(and) killing our workers and supporters all over the country," local reporters quoted Khaleda as saying.
The BNP walked out of parliament on Sunday, saying the Awami League prevented its opponents from exercising their rights in parliament.

Khaleda on Monday criticised a bill introduced that proposed the repeal of a 1975 law preventing the trial of killers of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, the country's independence leader and father of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
Mujib, who led Bangladesh to independence from Pakistan in 1971, was gunned down with most of his family in 1975.
Mujib's successors protected themselves from prosecution with an indemnity ordinance.
Khaleda said: "If there has to be a trial, they (government) must go for trial of those responsible for thousands of deaths (which) occurred during 1971-1975 (when Mujib was in power)."
